sections.text: Vowels (a, e, i, o, u) have two main sounds. Short vowels are quick and clipped: a as in cat, e as in pen, i as in sit, o as in pot, u as in sun. Long vowels say their own name: a as in cake, e as in bee, i as in bike, o as in cone, u as in cube. A silent e at the end (like cake, bike, cone) usually makes the vowel long. In closed syllables (like cat, sit), the vowel stays short. Y can sometimes act as a vowel.
Consonants are the other letters of the alphabet. Each makes a distinct sound that shapes words. Listen to the first sound in each word below — that's the consonant sound.
Say each consonant sound out loud, then think of one word that starts with it.
Short a says /a/ like in apple — when a single vowel is boxed in between two consonants, it usually keeps this quick, clipped sound instead of saying its name.
Say each word out loud and listen for this pattern.
